claim: Title: OpenAI hardened GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol against reasoning-trace extraction.

support.quote: With GPT‑6.2 Astra and GPT‑6.2 Sol, we tie a model’s protected reasoning to the conversation history that produced it.

claim: Red-teaming cut prior-turn leaks from 54.0% to 0.2% and weekly enforcement reaches tens of thousands of accounts.

support.quote: The average attack success rate fell from 54.0% against GPT‑6 Astra with its original safeguards to 0.2% against GPT‑6.2 Astra with its updated safeguards.
Our weekly enforcement actions against these campaigns have ranged in scale from thousands to tens of thousands of accounts, with the rate increasing significantly this past summer.

claim: OpenAI published its report on adversarial distillation on November 20, 2026.

support.quote: Through adversarial distillation, a second model can learn advanced frontier capabilities without inheriting the safeguards that govern how the original model can use them.

note: Publication date 2026-11-20 is recorded in sources.json for the primary source.

claim: Average success of extracting protected reasoning from an earlier request fell from 54.0% to 0.2% across six attacker models.

support.quote: The average attack success rate fell from 54.0% against GPT‑6 Astra with its original safeguards to 0.2% against GPT‑6.2 Astra with its updated safeguards.

The adaptive black-box evaluation aggregates results across six attacker models, with automated red-teamers adjusting their approach as the system responds and seeing only what an external user would see.

claim: Current-request extraction fell from 22.9% to 0.9%.

support.quote: For extraction from the current request, the corresponding average fell from 22.9% to 0.9%, OpenAI reports.
In internal automated tests, attacks pulling protected reasoning from prior requests dropped from a 54.0 percent success rate on GPT-6 Astra to 0.2 percent on GPT-6.2 Astra.

claim: Adversarial distillation can transfer frontier capabilities without the original safeguards.

support.quote: Through adversarial distillation, a second model can learn advanced frontier capabilities without inheriting the safeguards that govern how the original model can use them.

claim: OpenAI fine-tuned identical student models on coding and defensive cybersecurity trajectories.

support.quote: After supervised fine-tuning, the student trained on exact reasoning traces generally outperformed the student trained on reasoning summaries.

after a round of reinforcement learning, the exact-trace student still scored higher at the largest inference budget tested on ExploitBench and SEC-bench Pro, while the summary-trained student did better at lower budgets

claim: One student used summaries and tool interactions, the other also exact reasoning traces.

support.quote: After supervised fine-tuning, the student trained on exact reasoning traces generally outperformed the student trained on reasoning summaries.

After reinforcement learning, the exact-trace student still scored higher at the largest inference budget tested on both benchmarks shown, while the summary-trained student scored higher at lower budgets.

claim: Anthropic reported 80.4% with full transcripts versus 71.8% with summaries.

support.quote: When training on the full transcripts, the distilled model achieved 80.4%; with only the summarized transcripts, it achieved 71.8%.

claim: OpenAI uses input and output classifiers covering assistant messages and tool-call arguments.

support.quote: We use input classifiers to detect attempts to extract protected reasoning, and output classifiers to detect leaks of protected reasoning in assistant messages and tool-call arguments.

claim: Scanning tool arguments catches protected reasoning leaked inside a tool call.

support.quote: We use input classifiers to detect attempts to extract protected reasoning, and output classifiers to detect leaks of protected reasoning in assistant messages and tool-call arguments.

note: Follows from the classifiers covering tool-call arguments.

claim: A September 30, 2026 disclosure preceded closing a path exposing encrypted reasoning across boundaries.

support.quote: The operators did not break our encryption, compromise a database, or gain direct access to stored user conversations.
With GPT‑6.2 Astra and GPT‑6.2 Sol, we tie a model’s protected reasoning to the conversation history that produced it.

note: Dates come from source metadata; the closing of the path is described by OpenAI's report.

claim: GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol tie protected reasoning to conversation history and block older model families.

support.quote: With GPT‑6.2 Astra and GPT‑6.2 Sol, we tie a model’s protected reasoning to the conversation history that produced it.
We also prevent older model families with weaker safeguards from reading GPT‑6.2 Astra and Sol’s protected reasoning.

claim: Custom history edits trigger removals visible in input_transformations, while OpenAI compaction preserves reasoning items.

support.quote: If you use OpenAI compaction via /responses/compact or context_management, our systems retain subsequent reasoning items despite the prefix being changed.
Use input_transformations from the Responses API response to see which reasoning items the API removed from the input and why.

claim: Weekly enforcement actions ranged from thousands to tens of thousands of accounts.

support.quote: Our weekly enforcement actions against these campaigns have ranged in scale from thousands to tens of thousands of accounts, with the rate increasing significantly this past summer.

claim: OpenAI briefed Congress in February on DeepSeek and attributed a core part of a campaign to Moonshot-linked individuals; 16,000 requests from over 4,000 users on July 24 and 25, 2026.

support.quote: OpenAI said it briefed Congress in February on activity indicating DeepSeek was attempting to distill US frontier models, and in September attributed a core part of a reasoning-extraction campaign to individuals associated with Moonshot AI, the developer of Kimi

The earlier report described 16,000 attempted extraction requests from more than 4,000 users on July 24 and 25, 2026, attributed a core cluster to individuals associated with Moonshot AI, and said it was unclear whether all operators belonged to one actor.

claim: OpenAI said operators did not break encryption; a cluster of over 15,000 users was disrupted by July 28; attribution to one actor is unclear.

support.quote: The operators did not break our encryption, compromise a database, or gain direct access to stored user conversations.
Further investigation identified related prompt-pattern activity across a cluster of more than 15,000 users, which we fully disrupted by July 28.
It is unclear whether all operators we observed during the relevant time period originated from a single actor.

claim: explainx.ai observed that the figures are vendor statements, not third-party audits.

support.quote: OpenAI treats unauthorized distillation as a frontier safety problem, not a licensing dispute alone.

note: Characterization of explainx.ai's commentary; its quotation addresses framing only. The point is also true by construction: all figures originate in OpenAI's own report.

claim: Anthropic reports banning tens of thousands of accounts and 90-99% reductions; updated policies effective November 20, 2026; OpenAI backs three bills.

support.quote: also banning tens of thousands of accounts to curb the theft of internal reasoning, reportedly succeeding in 90 to 99 percent of cases.
Early evidence suggests that these methods have reduced the amount of data harvested by distillers by around 90 to 99%.
We’re also updating our Usage Policies, effective November 20, 2026, to clarify the rules for safe model development and sensitive uses of AI.
We’ve also told Congress we support the Chip Security Act, the AI OVERWATCH Act, and the MATCH Act.

claim: Anthropic's October 12, 2026 report says bans often come within two hours and it turned away meaningful revenue and trillions of tokens of traffic.

support.quote: We’ve used these defenses to ban tens of thousands of accounts associated with distillation, often in less than two hours after such an account begins a distillation campaign.
We’ve turned away meaningful revenue and trillions of tokens’ worth of paying traffic from distillers, and our research and product teams have invested substantial time and effort into this problem.

claim: OpenAI's October 21, 2026 policy introduced SafetyIDs without revealing user identities.
